items.description: Sec. 4 and the abstract say only '16 × 32 square elements' (Sec. 6: 'rectangular design domain'). They don't say which count runs along the span (support to load) and which along the depth. The figures that would show this (Figs. 10–12) aren't available. Table 1's H×W notation and the usual 2:1 cantilever suggest 16 high × 32 long, but this is never stated.
readings: Span (clamped edge to loaded free edge) = 32 elements, depth = 16 elements (16 rows × 32 columns)
Span = 16 elements, depth = 32 elements (deep cantilever clamped along a 32-element edge)

items.entity: Physical element size / domain size and out-of-plane thickness
items.description: Sec. 4 gives only element counts and says units were omitted. No element side length or thickness is given. For square 2D elements the side length does not change K. Thickness scales the stiffness, so compliance scales by 1/t.
readings: Unit square elements, unit thickness (domain 32 × 16 length units)
Other element size or thickness (e.g., t = 0.1); compliance scales by 1/t

items.description: Sec. 4 gives 'Poisson's ratio ν = 1.0'. That value is inadmissible for an isotropic linear-elastic solid: the plane-stress factor 1/(1−ν²) becomes singular, and plane strain/3D require ν < 0.5. It must be a typo, and the value actually used is unknown.
readings: ν = 0.3 (usual SIMP benchmark value)

items.entity: 2D stress state of the FE model
items.description: The FEM description (Secs. 2.2.1, 4) never says plane stress or plane strain. Plane strain is equivalent to a different effective E and ν.
readings: Plane stress
Plane strain

items.description: Only 'square elements' and FEM are mentioned (Secs. 2.2.1, 4). The element type and integration are not given. The shear-locking/checkerboard remark in Sec. 3.2.4 hints at bilinear Q4.
readings: 4-node bilinear quadrilateral (Q4), 2×2 Gauss integration
8-node serendipity quadrilateral (Q8)
Q4 with incompatible modes

items.description: Sec. 4 ('we choose the cantilever') and Sec. 6 ('cantilever beam') don't say which edge is supported or whether the whole edge or only some nodes are restrained. Left vs right is only a mirror image. Sec. 3.2.1's bar-system description mentions 'the support point', which leaves a point or partial support possible.
readings: All nodes of one end edge (e.g., the full left edge) restrained
Only part of the end edge restrained (e.g., the two corner nodes or a central segment)

items.description: No text says which displacement components are fixed. 'Cantilever' implies a fully clamped edge, but this is not stated.
readings: Both ux and uy fixed at every support node (clamped)
Only the span-direction (normal) displacement fixed along the edge, plus one node fixed transversely (roller-type wall)

items.entity: Load application point on the free end
items.description: Sec. 4 gives no load location. The mid-depth tip load and the corner tip load are both common cantilever benchmarks.
readings: Mid-depth node of the free end edge
Bottom corner node of the free end edge (top corner is the mirror image)

items.description: Not stated whether a single nodal force or a distributed traction is used. Sec. 3.2.1 talks of bars joining 'the support point and the load point', which hints at a point load, but nothing is said for the Sec. 4 example itself.
readings: Single nodal point force
Force spread over a few nodes around the load point
Uniform shear traction along the whole free edge

items.description: No load direction is given anywhere. For a single load the sign does not matter, because compliance is quadratic in the load. Whether the load is transverse or axial does matter.
readings: Transverse to the span (e.g., vertical, downward)
Parallel to the span (axial)

items.description: No force magnitude is given. Table 3 reports 'dimensionless compliance' (initial 5,974; SIMP 1,294; proposed 1,287). These absolute values depend on F² and on thickness or normalization. A rough estimate with unit load and unit thickness gives much smaller values, so an unreported magnitude or normalization may have been used. Only ratios are comparable.
readings: |F| = 1 (unit load)
Unreported magnitude/normalization; compare only compliance ratios (initial/optimal ≈ 4.6)

items.description: Sec. 4: 'evenly distributed density over the design area (see Fig. 10)'. The value appears only in Fig. 10. Table 3 (initial compliance ≈ 4.6× the optimum, so the start cannot be fully solid) points to 0.5, but no value is stated.
readings: x_e = 0.5 (= volume fraction) everywhere
x_e = 1.0 everywhere (solid start)

items.entity: Sensitivity/density (mesh-independence) filter in the OC loop (previous SIMP)
items.description: Sec. 2.3 adopts only post-processing (Eq. (7) thresholding and floating-island removal) and gives no checkerboard or sensitivity filter or radius for the iterations. Appendix 1 says hole filling 'remarkably increases' the area of the SIMP result, which hints at an unfiltered, hole-rich raw design.
readings: No sensitivity or density filter (raw OC)
Sensitivity filter, rmin = 1.5 element widths
Sensitivity filter, rmin = 2.0 element widths
Density filter, rmin = 1.5 element widths

items.entity: OC move limit m and damping coefficient η
items.description: Eqs. (5)–(6) and the Nomenclature define m and η, but no values are given. They matter because results are taken after a fixed 40 updates.
Sec. 2.2.1 says a lower limit xmin is set for numerical stability but gives no value. It is also needed for void stiffness when evaluating the filtered 0/1 designs in Table 3.
readings: xmin = 0.001
xmin = 0.01

items.entity: Stopping criterion / number of OC updates
items.description: Sec. 2.4 step 5 (and Sec. 3.2 step 5) iterate 'until the difference between x_new and x falls below a certain value' (no tolerance given). The Fig. 11 caption and Table 2 instead report results after 40 iterations/density updates for both methods.
readings: Stop after exactly 40 OC updates
Iterate until max|x_new − x| < 0.01
Iterate until max|x_new − x| < 0.001

items.entity: Threshold θ of Eq. (7) (previous-method post-processing, Fig. 11(b))
items.description: Sec. 2.3 sets θ only implicitly, so that the volume of the proposed-method result 'is close to' the thresholded SIMP volume. Neither θ nor the matched volume is reported, and the filtered volumes need not be 50%.
readings: θ chosen so the thresholded design has exactly 50% volume
θ chosen to match the (unreported) solid-element count of the proposed method's filtered design

items.description: Sec. 2.3 points to Sec. 3.2.4.1, which defines floating islands only as material 'not connected to any other elements regarded as material'. The connectivity rule (edge or corner contact) is not specified. It is also unclear whether whole detached clusters or only isolated single elements are removed.
readings: Remove every solid cluster not edge-connected (4-neighbour) to the main structure joining support and load
Same, but with 8-neighbour (corner) connectivity
Remove only single solid elements that have no solid neighbour

items.description: Sec. 2.4 step 6 applies the filtering once, after convergence. Sec. 5.2.1, however, blames a compliance rise near update 30 in Fig. 13(b) on the filtering, which implies filtering inside the loop. Sec. 3.2.3 also speaks of filtering 'with the optimum structure generated by the CNN as the initial structure'.
readings: Filter once after the final (40th) update
Filter after every OC update and continue iterating from the filtered design

items.description: Sec. 3.2.4.2 keeps holes 'larger than a certain size' but never gives the size. Also unspecified: the binarization threshold for the CNN-OC densities, whether islands→holes→peninsulas are applied once or repeated, and how the 'check for checkerboard' in Sec. 3.2.4 is decided. The peninsula rule (≤2 of 8 neighbours solid) is the only part that is defined.
readings: Binarize at 0.5; fill enclosed voids of 1 element; one pass islands→holes→peninsulas
Binarize at 0.5; fill enclosed voids up to 4 elements; one pass
Binarize at 0.5; fill voids up to 4 elements; repeat the three operations until no change

items.description: Fig. 11(c),(d) use CNN-estimated sensitivities (Secs. 3.2.1–3.2.2, Table 1). Only the Adam hyperparameters are given. Missing: kernel sizes, activations, final fully-connected layer size, loss, training-set size and bar-system generation parameters, epochs/batch size, and initial weights. Different trainings give different layouts (Sec. 5.3.2, Fig. 14). A standard solver would use exact FE sensitivities instead.
readings: Use exact FE (adjoint) sensitivities; this reproduces only the previous-method results Fig. 11(a),(b)
Train a Table-1 CNN with assumed settings (e.g., 3×3 flat kernels, 2×2 stride-2 down/up kernels, ReLU, MSE loss) on self-generated bar-system samples
